q: Clerkage / Cancellation charges are booked under ______.

q: Revenue from Platform Tickets are booked under _______.
e: The correct answer is Other Coaching Revenue. Revenue from platform tickets is a charge for use of station premises, not a fare for travel, so it is booked under Other Coaching Revenue. Like clerkage and cancellation charges, it is a coaching-related receipt that does not belong to Passenger Revenue. The exam linkage to remember is that both platform tickets and clerkage/cancellation charges fall under Other Coaching Revenue.

q: Positive Amount of Traffic suspense reflect ______.

options.B: Amount of Debit Raised is more than Realisation of Debits.
options.C: Amount of Realisation of Debit is more than amount of Debit Raised.

e: This question turns on a precise definition — here is the reasoning. A positive amount of traffic suspense reflects both efficiency of the Traffic Accounts Office and a position where realisation of debits exceeds the debits raised. When credits (realisations) outpace the debits booked, the suspense balance turns positive. Traffic suspense temporarily holds unadjusted traffic transactions (like unconnected earnings) pending final allocation.

q: Various components of Traffic Suspense are

options.B: AOB, Cash in Transit & Demands Recoverable.

e: Option C (Both (A) & (B).) is the correct choice. Traffic suspense comprises both station outstanding on one side and AOB, cash in transit and demands recoverable on the other. Station outstanding covers unrealised station earnings, while AOB, cash in transit and demands recoverable cover other unrealised traffic dues. Together these components make up the gross traffic suspense awaiting realisation. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: Higher Yearly Target of Traffic Suspense by Railway Board reflects

options.A: There is large accumulation of unrealised Revenue
options.B: There is less accumulation of unrealised Revenue
options.C: There needs to be more clearance in the year.

e: The logic behind the correct choice is explained below. A higher yearly target of traffic suspense fixed by the Railway Board reflects a large accumulation of unrealised revenue and the need for greater clearance during the year. The target is set higher precisely because past unrealised balances are heavy. Traffic suspense temporarily holds unadjusted traffic transactions (like unconnected earnings) pending final allocation.

q: Which of the formula is correct ?

options.A: Gross Traffic Revenue + Traffic suspense = Gross Traffic s Receipt
options.B: Gross Traffic Receipts – Gross Traffic Revenue = Traffic Suspense
options.C: Gross Traffic Revenue + Amount Debited to Traffic Suspense – Amount Credited to Traffic Suspense = Gross Traffic Receipts

e: Only (A) & (B) — that is the right answer. Both formula (A) and formula (B) are correct because they are algebraic rearrangements of the same relationship: Gross Traffic Receipts equals Gross Traffic Revenue plus Traffic Suspense. Formula (A) states this directly, and formula (B) restates it as receipts minus revenue equals suspense. Formula (C) is not the correct relationship, so only (A) and (B) stand. The principle behind this is worth grasping, not just memorising: once you understand why the rule is framed this way, the answer follows naturally instead of needing rote recall.

q: Credit Advice Note is ______.

e: A clear grasp of the concept makes this question straightforward. Both Abstract X and Abstract Y are forwarded to the Railway Board every month. q: Net Result of Apportionment forms part of _______ of Traffic Books
e: The logic behind the correct choice is explained below. The net result of apportionment forms part of Part B of the Traffic Books. Apportionment distributes through-traffic earnings among the railways that carried the traffic, and Part B is the section of the Traffic Books devoted to this. q: Position of Station balance sheet is consolidated in ________ of Traffic Books

q: Station Balance sheet reflects the following
e: A clear grasp of the concept makes this question straightforward. The station balance sheet reflects collected revenue, that is, the earnings actually collected at the stations. It is distinct from apportioned revenue, which is the home railway's share after inter-railway distribution, and from originating revenue. The station balance sheet summarises a station's earnings, remittances and outstanding at month-end for traffic accounting.

q: The period for completion of Accounts is
e: Option A (Complete Calendar Month.) is the correct choice. The period for completion of accounts is the complete calendar month. q: At Station it is the duty of Chief Booking supervisor, CNC & SM.

options.A: To get the debit admitted by staff responsible as soon as Error sheet is received.
options.B: Simply return the all Error Sheet.
options.C: Give remarks for all Not Admitted Debits.

e: The correct answer is (A) and (C) only. At the station, the Chief Booking Supervisor, CNC and Station Master must get the debit admitted by the staff responsible as soon as the error sheet is received, and must give remarks for all not-admitted debits. Prompt admission keeps the debit from lingering, while remarks on not-admitted debits let the Accounts Office pursue or drop them. This station-level follow-up feeds directly into recovery of admitted debits through salary or cash deposit. Notice how precisely the correct option is worded.

options.C: On vouchers Tendered by Post and Telegraph Department for occasional Despatches for conveyance of mail.

A tender is a formal offer to supply/execute at quoted rates; railways invite open tenders to ensure competition and transparency. q: No inter Railway Adjustment should be carried for

options.C: Overcharge sheets relating to clearance of Stations Outstanding

No inter-railway adjustment is carried out for public claims refunds, items twice accounted for, or overcharge sheets relating to clearance of station outstanding. These items are settled within the home railway's own books rather than through the inter-railway settlement machinery. Keeping them out of inter-railway adjustment avoids unnecessary cross-railway accounting.

q: Which formula is correct.

options.A: Cash in Transit = Balance of Cash for a month as per General s Books – Balance of Cash for a month as per Traffic Books.
options.B: Cash in Transit = Cash for a month with Chief Cashier – Cash for a month as per Traffic Books.
options.C: Cash in Transit =Total Cash collected as per Balance sheet Section- Cash for a month as per Traffic Books.

e: The correct answer is Cash in Transit = Balance of Cash for a month as per General s Books – Balance of Cash for a month as per Traffic Books.. Cash in transit equals the balance of cash for a month as per the General Books minus the balance of cash for the month as per the Traffic Books. The difference arises from timing: cash accounted in one set of books but not yet in the other. The same principle verifies the correctness of the Traffic Book, where traffic accounts under Traffic Books minus those under General Books equals cash in transit.

e: The correct answer is Part D. The final journal entry recording traffic revenue under various categories into the General Books forms part of Part D of the Traffic Books. The first reconciles the timing difference between the two books, while the second confirms inter-railway balances. Together they prove the Traffic Book balances.

q: Minimum Balance in AOB reflects

options.A: Carriage Bills section is working very efficiently in timely s raising of Bills and recovery of same.
options.B: Carriage Bills section is working very slow and not raising Bills.
options.C: Booking against vouchers has gone down.

e: The correct answer is Both (A) &( C). A minimum balance in AOB reflects both an efficiently working Carriage Bills section, which raises bills and recovers them in time, and a fall in booking against vouchers. Prompt billing and recovery keep unrealised bills low, while fewer voucher bookings mean fewer pending items. Together these two factors keep the AOB closing balance at its minimum.
